newsitem.title: GERMANY: New round of German construction wage talks starts.
newsitem.headline: New round of German construction wage talks starts.

text.p: Negotiators in the third round of wage talks for the 1.3 million workers in the German construction industry said before entering talks on Tuesday they saw little hope for an overall deal.

Both union officials and employers said there was little chance of finding agreement in one of the key areas of talks, measures to prevent the upsurge in unemployment that occurs each winter as building projects are halted by poor weather.
Peter Huber, chief negotiator for the employers' side, said that if no agreement could be reached by Wednesday, the employers would seek arbitration in the matter.

Already this year, winter construction unemployment is calculated to have accounted for nearly half of the 510,000 jump in January joblessness that has since taken overall German unemployment levels to post-war records.

That was itself partly a result of a government move last winter to scrap "poor weather" payments to building employees last winter which allowed them to be retained by their firms even when there was no work.
In their place, employer and union representatives were obliged to negotiate agreements under which firms pay their staff "bridging money" in times of poor weather.

But these bridging agreements have since proved too expensive for firms and the vast majority do not pay them, preferring instead to lay off staff during winter and later using cheaper foreign labour.
IG Bau, the construction trade union, has not yet named a definite wage demand in the talks, saying only that it wants to ensure that construction worker salaries do not fall in real terms.
